CONIC SECTIONS: ELLIPSES AND HYPERBOLAS
The term conic section refers to the shapes that result from intersecting a right circular cone with a plane.
INTRODUCTIONM
The ancient Greeks studied conic sections thousands of years ago, yet these studies continue to provide a basis for modern technological advances.
Planets and satellites follow an elliptical orbit. The path of alpha particles in the electric field of an atom's nucleus is described using hyperbolas.

LESSON MENU
An ellipse is formed when the plane is tilted as it passes through the cone.
DISCUSSION
An ellipse has two axes of symmetry........................
The major axis passes lengthwise through the center (C) of the ellipse.
An ellipse has two vertices (V1, V2) at the intersection of the major axis.
The two foci (F1, F2) are located within the ellipse on the major axis.
The minor axis passes through the center and is perpendicular to the major axis.
An ellipse can be drawn by tying a piece of string to the foci and using a pencil to pull the string taut while rotating it around the foci.
The length of the string is constant since it does not change.
We can also say that the string length represents the sum of the distances from the two foci to any point (P) on the ellipse.
The sum of these distances is constant since the string length is constant.
An ellipse is the set of all points in a plane whose distances from two fixed points, called the foci, have a constant sum.
